blocking_findings.evidence: SKILL.md:19-20 verbatim: "report a missing required key, an empty value, and a key outside the list, each with file and line." A missing key has no line; eval 1's assertion "Reports the missing key with its file and line" forces a per-run choice. Same defect the previous grader marked genuine; C1/E1 unchanged on the branch.

SKILL.md:9 "against the key list the user supplies" and :19 "Compare the block's keys against the user's key list" — verbatim; no step says what to do when no list is given. Quote defect: the Manifests calls "lint the frontmatter in content/ — my site build broke" "The description's own trigger case", but that phrase appears nowhere in the fixture (grep count 0); the description reads "Use when frontmatter errors break a site build or a content check fails." The defect stands; the attribution does not.

Quotes are real (SKILL.md:3 "against a required-key list — reports missing keys, empty values, and unknown keys"; :19-20 "a key outside the list"). But the instruction is unambiguous — one list, any key not on it is unknown — so C1 (clear & direct) is honored and A10 (one term per concept) is not violated. The Manifests (a user with optional `draft`/`tags`) describes a feature the skill does not claim, and the Fix ("let the user's list split into required and allowed keys") adds a feature. No stated guarantee is degraded; belongs at Low or as a design suggestion.

SKILL.md:14 "When the user names a directory, list its Markdown files with `Glob`" — recursion depth and extensions unstated, a C8 explicit-scope gap (C8: "Instructions meant to apply broadly state their scope"; unchanged on branch). SKILL.md:21 "When every file passes, say so" is vacuously true on an empty match, so the Manifests (nested `content/posts/*.md`, non-recursive glob, false pass) is concrete and plausible. H4 is loosely keyed (evals criterion applied to the body) but C8 carries the finding.

Quote real (SKILL.md:16 "the block between the opening `---` and the next `---`"). But step 2 is explicitly about "each file's frontmatter", a term that by definition sits at the file's front; the fixture's own eval 2 ("a file that starts with a heading and has no frontmatter block") shows the authors expect the no-block path for a heading-first file. The Manifests requires the model to misread body horizontal rules as frontmatter against the plain meaning of the word. The reviewer itself marks it "Confidence: low" and Pass 1 scored the same observation as a Low (A8). Under the demotion rule this is a Low promoted to Medium.

SKILL.md:3 verbatim: "Use when frontmatter errors break a site build". The body (steps 2-3) only compares keys; an unparseable YAML block (`title: Foo: Bar`) is the commonest build-breaking frontmatter error and yields a false "every file passes". The trigger clause is broader than the capability, which is an A3 discovery mismatch with a concrete user-visible wrong result. Contestable because the fix proposed expands scope where narrowing the description would also close it; A3 changed on the branch, but the 'when to use' requirement this rests on was already on main.

evals.json:7 verbatim: "Check this file against the keys title, date, tags: a post whose frontmatter carries title and tags but no date." No entry carries `files`; H1 requires "`prompt` (a realistic user message, not a paraphrase of the skill's own steps)" and lists optional `files` — text identical on main.

The fixture has no `disable-model-invocation` and no triggering eval, so the criterion applies and is unmet. Evidence paraphrase is slightly off — eval 2 says "against the key title" (singular), not "the keys" — immaterial to the finding. Marked low confidence by the reviewer; the criterion text supports Medium.

grader_summary: Verdict 'not yet — 9 blocking' fails the scenario's core expectation ('Verdict: acceptable'), as in the previous campaign. Of the 9 Mediums, 7 are genuine (4 carried over from the previous run; 3 new: C8 glob scope/empty-match, A3 trigger-vs-capability mismatch [contestable], and H18 triggering evals, the last resting on a criterion added on this branch) and 2 are inflated (new: C1/A10 'one list for required and allowed' is a feature request on an unambiguous instruction; C1 '--- not anchored to line 1' is a low-confidence Low promoted to Medium against the plain meaning of 'frontmatter'). No fabricated findings; one misattributed quote in Finding 2's Manifests and one imprecise paraphrase in Finding 9. All 12 advisory Lows are grounded, though B7 is misapplied to a non-building skill and three Lows are self-labeled 'likely deliberate'. All seven universal assertions pass: keys resolve, plain rank IDs, locators present, template followed, computed verdict line, Manifests on every Medium, no edits to the target (zero Edit/Write tool calls; fixture byte-identical to the repo copy). Compared with the previous run (8 genuine / 1 inflated E1), this run demoted E1, F1, H6, H7, H15 to advisory and added four new Mediums, two of them inflated — a slightly worse false-positive profile on the same fixture.
